conditionalFormatting API used: Not supported in Office JS add-ins. Apply formatting explicitly in a loop: values.forEach((row,i) => { if (condition) sheet.getRange(addr).format.font.color = '#hex'; })
Array dimensions do not match range size: Count range rows×cols carefully. A range of R rows × C cols needs a 2-D array of exactly R inner arrays each with C elements. BAD: 2-row range with [[a,b],[c,d],[e,f]]. GOOD: [[a,b],[c,d]]
autofit() called instead of autofitColum: The correct method is autofitColumns(), not autofit(). BAD: range.getEntireColumn().autofit(). GOOD: range.getEntireColumn().format.autofitColumns()
getRange called on a Range object instea: getRange() is a Worksheet method, not a Range method. BAD: range.getRange('A1'). GOOD: sheet.getRange('A1')
getRow() used to access row formatting: Range has no getRow() method. To format a specific row use sheet.getRange('A'+rowNum+':Z'+rowNum) or index into the range with getCell(rowIndex, colIndex). BAD: range.getRow(0).fill.color. GOOD: sheet.getRange('A1:Z1').format.fill.color
numberFormat assigned plain string on mu: Wrap in a 2-D array matching the range dimensions: range.numberFormat = [['$#,##0','$#,##0'],['$#,##0','$#,##0']]
values assigned 1-D array: Excel JS API requires a 2-D array: range.values = [['a','b'],['c','d']]
Missing await ctx.sync(): Call await ctx.sync() at least once before the function returns to flush all queued operations
getRange with hard-coded very large row: Avoid row numbers > 1048576; use dynamic range addressing instead
forEach loop with multiple ctx.sync insi: Batch all range operations first, then call ctx.sync() once at the end — multiple syncs inside a loop are slow and error-prone
load() called after ctx.sync(): Call range.load('values') BEFORE ctx.sync(); values are only populated after the sync
